title: Causes of WW1 Adventure
welcome_lead: Why did the world go to war in 1914? Meet the MAIN causes and the spark that set Europe on fire. 🎯
meta_desc: WW1 Causes Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of MAIN causes and the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
final_note: You met the MAIN causes (Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism) and the trigger of June 1914.

concepts.def: Building up armies and glorifying war
Countries promising to defend each other
Strong pride in one's own country

walkthroughs.body_html:
By 1914 Europe was a tinderbox. Historians remember the long-term causes with the word MAIN:

  • Militarism — countries built huge armies and navies.
  • Alliances — Europe was split into two armed camps.
  • Imperialism — countries competed for empires.
  • Nationalism — proud pride in one's own country and people.

A small spark could set it all off. 🔥

Europe was divided into two big alliances:

  • The Triple Entente — Britain, France and Russia.
  • The Triple Alliance — Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy.

Britain and Germany were locked in a naval arms race, building giant battleships called Dreadnoughts.

On 28 June 1914, Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand visited Sarajevo in Bosnia.

A Serbian nationalist, Gavrilo Princip, shot him and his wife dead.

Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia. Russia backed Serbia. Germany backed Austria. France and Britain backed Russia. Within weeks, the alliances dragged most of Europe into war. ⚔️

mcqs.q: Did the New Deal end the Great Depression?
options: Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
It eased unemployment and restored confidence but did not end the Depression — WWII spending did. Roosevelt's reforms reshaped American government permanently.
The New Deal was a treaty with Britain to share gold reserves.
Roosevelt's New Deal ended the Great Depression by 1936.

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles directly cause WWII?
options: Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
Versailles caused WWII directly because it was so harsh on Germany.
It contributed via German resentment and economic strain, but the 1930s Depression, Hitler's choices, and Allied appeasement were equally necessary — Versailles alone is not sufficient.
The New Deal was a treaty with Britain to share gold reserves.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine commit the US to in 1947?
options: The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
The Truman Doctrine declared war on the Soviet Union.
Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
Supporting free peoples resisting communist takeover — initially Greece and Turkey — formalising the policy of containment articulated by George Kennan.
